correctness.rationale: For the exact rectangular torus T=∏(R/a_i Z) with quotient l_infinity metric, independent Haar-uniform points induce independent U_i uniform on [0,c_i=a_i/2] in each shortest circular coordinate. D has the law max_i U_i, so F(t)=∏_i min(t/c_i,1). The small-t log-log slope recovers d; jumps of tF'/F at the thresholds recover every c_i and multiplicity, including the terminal jump. This is an injective metric-parameter reconstruction only within rectangular max-Finsler tori, not Euclidean quotient tori. On (0,b=max_i c_i), m(t)=tF'/F lies in {1,...,d}; F(t)/t^d is nonincreasing and F(t)/t is nondecreasing. Inverse quantile Q therefore has Q(u)/u^(1/d) nondecreasing and Q(u)/u nonincreasing. For p>q>0 interpolate positive increasing quantile functions A to B with B/A monotone via Z_t=A^(1−t) B^t. Derivative of log(E Z_t^p/(E Z_t^q)^(p/q)) is p times the difference of log(B/A) expectations under p- and q-size biased measures; monotone likelihood ratio makes it of the appropriate strict sign. This gives exact bounds [d/(d+p)]/[d/(d+q)]^(p/q) <= ratio < [1/(1+p)]/[1/(1+q)]^(p/q), lower equality precisely when all side lengths agree; degenerate lengths approaching zero give sharp unattained upper value. The p=2,q=1 bound becomes 1+1/[d(d+2)] <= E[D²]/(ED)² < 4/3. The pinned verify.py's exact piecewise CDF integration is consistent with this derivation; independent rational calculation of 205 sorted length profiles across d=2..6 confirmed samples. Neither finite checks nor citation to star ordering replaces the full quantile proof.
